title: Tahini halva
summary: A dense sesame confection of tahini beaten with hot syrup, studded with pistachios and set in a loaf tin.
steps: Line a 20 x 10 cm (8 x 4 in) loaf tin with parchment. Put the tahini, vanilla and salt in a bowl.
Heat the erythritol, allulose and water in a small pan, stirring until dissolved, then boil without stirring until it reaches 120 °C (250 °F).
Pour the hot syrup into the tahini and stir hard with a wooden spoon. Within a minute it will seize and thicken; keep stirring until it pulls away from the bowl, then fold in the pistachios.
Press firmly into the tin and smooth the top. Cool, then cover and leave 12 hours at room temperature or in the fridge before slicing.
tips: Real halva's flaky strands come from sugar crystallising as it is beaten; erythritol crystallises too and gives some of that texture, but expect something closer to a firm fudge.
Stop stirring as soon as it pulls together; overworking makes it oily.

origin.history: Halva is an old Arabic word for a sweet, applied across the Middle East, South Asia and the Balkans to many different confections. The tahini-based kind, made by beating sesame paste with a hot sugar syrup, became widespread across the Ottoman lands and remains the classic halva of Turkey, the Levant, Greece and the Balkans.
